Extract: gate first (429 / 503 store a degraded row and never call the provider), provider call outside any transaction, normalisation (ranges, grounding substring check, Arabic-Indic digits, image wording stripped of URLs, e-mails and phone runs and cut to 80 chars, SEC-7; non-USD budget -> unknown + question); every failure -> degraded with every field unknown

RS-01, RS-02, RS-03 (API part), RS-05 (pipeline incl. T10 DB-planted catalog text) and RS-39 tests named with their ids; the fake's image map is injected in tests so this task does not depend on the EXT-1 fixtures

DELETE /api/requests/:id: 409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS on the spec's status list, void rule for an active reservation (REQUEST_DELETED), hard delete when no supplier order existed, tombstone otherwise, audit event either way; retention sweep with a pinned clock (7 d + 1 min deleted, 6 d 23 h kept, audit event per image) started at startup and hourly in main.js
completedWork: ROUTES (src/routes/requests.js): POST /api/requests/:id/image (owner 404 first, declared type 415, Content-Length required 400 / over the cap 413, gate.takeRate 429, streamed body with cap and deadline, magic bytes 415, store), GET /api/requests/:id/image (detected type, nosniff, Content-Security-Policy: sandbox, Cache-Control: private, no-store, Content-Disposition inline), POST /api/requests/:id/extract, DELETE /api/requests/:id. SERVICE (src/services/extraction.js): createAiRuntime builds the provider through selectProvider (the fake whenever RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, labelled fallback when an adapter is missing) and the gate from gateLimitsFromConfig; takeModelFault reads and decrements the fake_model:* row of fault_flags (name '<kind>:<fault>', remaining count or NULL) and the fake gets it as faults(); saveImage writes a random 128-bit name to uploads/.tmp with mode 0600, renames, then replaces any earlier image in one transaction and audits; extractRequest runs gate.run (rate, concurrency, budget reserved before the call, settled after) with the provider call outside any transaction, a watchdog at RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS (charged at the cap), structural re-validation, and then normaliseExtraction (ranges; grounding substring check with NFC, whitespace and Arabic-Indic digit folding; image provenance without an image downgraded; non-USD wording makes the budget unknown plus the server-template question; image wording stripped of URLs, e-mail addresses and phone runs and cut to 80; a bare HH:MM deadline gets the request's Asia/Amman day). A gate refusal (429 / 503) stores a degraded row in a separate transaction, never calls the provider, and rethrows the gate's error with details {...gate details, degraded: true, extraction}; any provider failure is 200 with degraded: true, schemaOk false, errorCode PROVIDER_TIMEOUT | PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE | PROVIDER_BAD_OUTPUT | PROVIDER_BUSY and every field unknown. A refusal by rate is stored as PROVIDER_BUSY, by budget as PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE. A degraded row replaces a degraded row that is already the newest, so a retry loop cannot grow the table. DELETE (src/services/requests.js deleteRequest): 409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS on the spec's seven operation states, an executing version or a reconciling reservation; otherwise approved versions go through markNonExecutable(REQUEST_DELETED), i.e. the void rule; hard delete (cascade) when no supplier order or reservation ever existed, tombstone otherwise (deleted_at, raw_text NULL, images and extractions deleted, replan_queue row removed, originalWording nulled in every requirements version, plan/order/payment/provider-call rows kept); image files unlinked after the commit; audit event request.delete either way. Confirm provenance (SEC-8) already behaved as specified in requests.js buildFields; it is now covered by tests. RETENTION (src/services/retention.js): runRetentionSweep deletes images with created_at <= now - RS_IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS (row, file, audit image.retention_delete per image), orphan files older than one day (only names this service generates; audit image.orphan_delete), rate_events older than 24 h and request_create older than 48 h (FU-20), and settles model_spend rows still reserved after 2 x RS_MODEL_TIMEOUT_MS at their cap; startRetention runs it at startup and every RS_RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS (default hourly), unref'd; main.js starts it and stops it in close(). main.js also loads the real adapters only when configured (cliVersion() must find the binary), falls back to the labelled fake otherwise and then reports the provider that really runs in config.extractionProvider so labels and /api/config stay honest. app.js builds deps.ai by default (so the harness needs no change) and takes uploadDeadlineMs (default UPLOAD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 s). config.js adds modelCallCapMicroUsd, modelDailyBudgetMicroUsd and fakeModelCostMicroUsd, parsed from the decimal string of the existing variables by string arithmetic. view.js: renderExtraction adds addressedToAssistant and hides the reserved __meta key; RequestView gets capabilities: {deleteRequest: true}. CONTRACT DELTAS (additive, for the spec / contract owner): (1) Extraction.addressedToAssistant: boolean on every Extraction (extract response, error details.extraction, RequestView.extraction). The spec's Extraction object lacks it although the acceptance criterion and the AI/LLM Design name the notice; the extractions table has no column, so the flag lives in fields_json under the reserved key __meta and renderExtraction removes it (rows written without it read as false). (2) RequestView.capabilities: {deleteRequest: true}. (3) The catalog has no code for a missing Content-Length or for an upload that misses its deadline, so both are 400 BAD_REQUEST (the deadline one with details.reason = UPLOAD_TIMEOUT and Connection: close). (4) A degraded row stored for a refusal carries errorCode PROVIDER_BUSY (rate and concurrency) or PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE (budget). (5) A new degraded row replaces a degraded row that is already the newest.

FU-2 IS ONLY PARTLY MET: the route enforces its own upload deadline while it streams (default UPLOAD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 s, injectable as createApp uploadDeadlineMs; test 'PB-3: ...' proves a stalled body ends as 400 with no file in uploads/ or .tmp). But Node's server-wide requestTimeout (30 s, src/http/server.js) still closes a slow upload first, so the effective cap is 30 s. Raising it means changing the server timeout, and test/unit/http/hardening.test.js (SEC-B-4) and test/unit/http/app.test.js (T19) assert 30000 for app.server.requestTimeout; neither file nor src/http/server.js is d3's. Orchestrator decision needed: accept 30 s as the effective limit, or have the owner of src/http/* raise it to 60 s together with those two assertions (a generic 30 s deadline for the non-upload routes would then have to move into the app).

NOTES FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) request ids come from INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after a hard delete of the highest id the next request reuses it, and audit rows of the deleted request share the id with the new one (found by my own test; a new migration with AUTOINCREMENT would fix it, migrations are not d3's). (2) A refusal by the budget or the rate limit stores a degraded row, as the spec says, and it is then the newest extraction: the page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable' even if an earlier extraction of the same request succeeded, and a later confirm treats every value as manual. (3) Uploads count toward the 10 per 10 minutes even when later refused by size or magic bytes (the count happens after the owner and header checks, before the body is read). (4) Sessions in tests that move the pinned clock more than 12 h must sign in again; the tests do.

lessonDecisions.note: The lesson's appliesWhen needs a hook or guard that maps file writes to a project root, or an implementer denied with 'has no claimed task' or 'outside the ownership' in a nested record. This task builds extraction routes, services and tests only, no hook, guard or root discovery, and the guard refused none of my writes, so none of its conditions holds.
